reason: Dk64 (50% state reduction) and the preregistered independent Dk96 fallback (25%) are structurally valid and execute on Ascend, but both fail the frozen GSM8K baseline-variability gate. Dk64 loses 0.202173 pp and Dk96 loses 0.303260 pp versus a baseline three-run range of 0.151630 pp. Dk96's serving means move favorably by only 0.33-0.44%, while all raw three-run intervals overlap. Neither treatment is adoptable for this frozen workload. Native profiling was intentionally not started because the quality gate failed.
allowed_claims: The official paper and code identity have been verified.
A local calibration adaptation is explicitly frozen and is not represented as FineWeb-Edu.
NPU4-7 were free at the recorded preflight.
The Dk64 treatment changes 48 linear-attention layers and executes head_k_dim=64 on Ascend.
The baseline and Dk64 performance arms each have three accepted 40/40 fixed-output repetitions.
Dk64 performance mean directions are favorable, but their repeated ranges overlap and stable separation is not established.
All six Dk64 quality repetitions are complete and independently hash/count/index audited.
Dk64 passes the LongBench-v2 gate but fails the GSM8K baseline-variability gate and is rejected for adoption.
The independent Dk96 checkpoint changes the same 48 linear-attention layers to head_k_dim=96 and passed structural and real-weight Ascend smoke audits.
The baseline and Dk96 performance arms each have three accepted 40/40 fixed-output repetitions; Dk96 mean directions are slightly favorable but every repeated range overlaps.
Dk96 LongBench-v2 has three complete, exact-index and hash-audited repetitions and passes its preregistered dataset gate.
Dk96 GSM8K has three complete, exact-index and hash-audited repetitions and fails its preregistered dataset gate.
The paper mechanism is feasible on this Qwen3.6/Ascend stack, but neither paper-exact reproduction nor a stable serving benefit was established.
The final evidence audit verified all expected artifacts and resource release.
forbidden_claims: DRRQR generally improves or preserves Qwen3.6-27B quality.
Dk64 establishes a stable Ascend serving improvement.
The paper's H100 training sequence-mixer 1.32x is directly comparable to this Ascend full-model serving experiment.
The absence of profiling after a failed quality gate proves anything about operator-level speed.
next_gate: No gate remains for this frozen experiment. Maintainer review may accept the rejection and knowledge proposals. LoRA recovery, another calibration corpus or another pruning ratio requires a new experiment identity.
